Baskerville42/outage-data-ua.description: A public repository of data on scheduled electricity outages in Ukraine.
Baskerville42/outage-data-ua.body:
# outage-data-ua

Public repository and tools for automatic collection, parsing, visualization (HTML), and automatic generation of PNG images of scheduled and emergency electricity outage charts in Ukraine.

The project retrieves data from public web pages of providers and stores it in JSON "as is" in the `data/` directory. This data is then displayed in a fixed HTML template and converted into PNG images, which are saved in `images/<region>/gpv-x-x.png`.

---

## Data format
Each region is stored in a file `data/<region>.json`. Basic structure (abridged):

```json
{
  "regionId": "kyiv",
  "regionAffiliation": "м. Київ",
  "lastUpdated": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z",
  "fact": { "updateFact": "06.11.2025 09:09" },
  "preset": { "updateFact": "04.11.2025 18:00" },
  "lastUpdateStatus": { "status": "parsed", "ok": true, "code": 200, "message": null, "at": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z", "attempt": 5 },
  "meta": { "schemaVersion": "1.0.0", "contentHash": "..." }
}
```

- `preset` — scheduled outages for the week for each group (weekly template). Stored "as is", without normalization of the structure.
- `fact` — actual/emergency outages for today and tomorrow for each group. Also…

BlackSlience-Reaper/egress-observatory.description: Egress: How good is your IP quality? It cross-scores multiple data sources and ASNs to help you clear obstacles in your Claude subscription environment!
BlackSlience-Reaper/egress-observatory.body:
# Egress · IP Purity Check

Open the page to detect your machine's outbound IP right away, and get a quality score that shows where every point was deducted.

**v2.0 · 2026-11-05**

[**Open website**](https://blackslience-reaper.github.io/egress-observatory/) · [Scoring rules](https://github.com/BlackSlience-Reaper/egress-observatory/blob/HEAD/SCORING.md) · [Data sources](https://github.com/BlackSlience-Reaper/egress-observatory/blob/HEAD/DATA-SOURCES.md) · [Browser extension](https://github.com/BlackSlience-Reaper/egress-observatory/blob/HEAD/browser-helper/README.md) · [Contributing](https://github.com/BlackSlience-Reaper/egress-observatory/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md)

Egress combines more than 20 IP databases, 16 DNS blocklists, 17 threat feeds, proxy and datacenter lists, same-/24 neighbors, and the reputation of the entire ASN. It then runs live tests using your current browser and network: WebRTC, DNS, TCP fingerprinting, IPv6, Cloudflare Turnstile, and Google reCAPTCHA.

- **Multi-source cross-checking**: the same underlying database counts for only one vote, to avoid duplicate voting.
- **Explainable results**: every deduction keeps its source and reason.
- **Updates as you go**: scores are recalculated as results arrive, and failed sources show their reasons one by one.
- **No account needed**: the page has no accounts or third-party analytics, and exported reports are generated locally in the browser. Shared-user estimates store only salted hashes (see [Privacy](#隐私)).

> Scores are estimates based on public data and do not represent any website's actual risk-control decisions.

## Usage

- Opening the page automatically detects your local outbound IP and runs a check. The **Check local outbound IP** button re-detects at any time (use it after switching proxy nodes).
- Enter any public IPv4 / IPv6 address to look up someone else's address. In this case only IP reputation is calculated, and live connection tests do not apply. `?ip=1.2.3.4` can be shared directly.
- **Hide IP** masks all addresses on the page for easier screenshots. **Export report** generates a local JSON file; when IPs are hidden, they are masked in the export too.

## What It Checks

| Section | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| IP intelligence databases | IPinfo (highest weight), Proxycheck, ip-api.com, IP2Location, DB-IP (via backend); IPLocate, GeoIPLookup, TechnikNews… |

Fish-under-sea/FISH-Dock.description: Everything is a Plugin · Windows AI desktop host: taskbar / Dynamic Island, Agent sessions and approvals, email, standalone plugin center, full-repository backup, and full/lightweight dual-package updates. Based on Wakuwaku, Rust + Tauri.
Fish-under-sea/FISH-Dock.body:
FISH Dock is a session and model workbench on the Windows desktop. It handles windows, the desktop island, runtime lifecycle, plugin pages, and the local data boundary. Concrete business features are loaded as plugins, which keeps the host clear, replaceable, and recoverable.

The desktop island displays session and approval status, and the workbench hosts email and plugin pages. Notifications, proxies, the model gateway, and model channels are provided on demand by separate plugins. Installing, enabling/disabling, and uninstalling are all managed uniformly by the host.

Capabilities the host provides itself. Business-side content (email, models, notifications, proxies) is loaded as plugins. For entry points and operations, see the next section, 'Workspace'.

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Settings page | Rearranged by spec into 5 pages (General / Agent / Appearance / Email / Plugins). The section order on each page is fixed. Regression tests compare directly against the spec file. |
| Plugin install & update | Verifies source, platform, and resource digest. Official plugins prefer npm (`@fish-under-sea/fish-dock-plugin-*`), then the npmmirror mirror, then GitHub Release. Install/update is a journaled transaction: interrupted runs can resume, and unverifiable runs are rolled back. After an update, only the current version is kept. Plugin cards have a unified three-state auto-start button: if enabled, it reads 'Disable auto-start'; if disabled, 'Start with Dock'; if the plugin has no auto-start capability, 'No auto-start needed' (display only). The only solid button on a card is 'Update'. Uninstall and 'Open plugin log' are grouped under 'More'. |
| About & announcements | On the About page, the brand image is centered at the top and clickable to open the official website (the address can be overridden at `url.official_site`). Update announcements show only the latest version and key new features, with full notes collapsed. Announcement sources are tried in order: GitHub, then Gitee, then local cache. If Gitee is not configured, it is explicitly skipped. Built-in updates are completed entirely inside the app. |
| Global hotkeys | The settings page can record key combinations. If a combination is taken by another program, a prompt is shown. If no usable combination is recorded within 30 seconds, recording is abandoned. |
| Appearance toolchain | Connects to your own installed Windhawk (since 2.1.2 the engine and compiler are no longer bundled). From the Appearance page you can import mods, compile, start/stop them, and restore them. |
| Theme & readability | Dark theme uses white text; light theme uses black text. The contrast audit (`scripts/check-contrast.mjs`) reports 0 violations. |
| Network & cache | Gallery and downloads go through a unified egress that respects proxy settings and falls back to a direct connection on failure. Tiered timeouts are configurable. The gallery LRU cache works offline. Email reconnection uses exponential backoff, a circuit breaker, and persisted state. |
| Memory | Hidden pages go idle: when a page is hidden, `IsVisible=false` is set and the memory target drops to Low. `check_quiet` no longer raises hidden pages back to normal. Plugin-page iframes are torn down entirely 5 minutes after being parked. The budget table for tiers A/B/C is in `红线-禁止屎山十条.md` (includes open items; see issue #29 / #30). |

This section covers only entry points and operations. For capability details, see the previous section.

## What it can do

A NovelAI image stores the prompt, every character, the negative prompt, and all the parameters from when it was made. NovelAI Prompt Studio reads them out so you can understand, organize, and edit them locally, then generate a new version with your own NovelAI account. Where each version came from and what changed are recorded automatically, and generated images go into the image library automatically.

| Read out | Organize | Generate | Keep |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drag in, paste, or open files; recognizes V4, V4.5, V5 | Prompts shown as blocks, and you can edit text directly like on a web page | Starts from this image's parameters, so you know the cost before generating | Generated images go into the image library automatically, one group per work |
| Separates what you wrote yourself from what NovelAI added automatically | Over 50,000 built-in Chinese translations, offline translation and classification | Queues, random pools, inpainting, outpainting, director tools | Search, filter, collections, export and share original images |

**Human and agent entry points.** Each capability is a single command. You use it in the UI, and agents such as Claude Code and Codex use the same set through the command-line tool `nai-studio`. Generations started by an agent require your confirmation before they are sent by default.

## Images made with it

The 24 images below were all generated in the software using V5, with original characters. The original images are in [`demo/images/showcase`](https://github.com/LBEILC/NovelAIPromptStudio/blob/HEAD/demo/images/showcase). The prompts, characters, and parameters are still stored in the images: download one and drag it into the software to see how it was written.

**Morning Bakery**

**Observatory Night**

**Umbrella Street in the Rainy Season**

**Summer Aquarium**

**Snowy Wayside Station**

**Neon Rooftop**

## Change it and generate, every version is remembered

After editing the prompt, click "Generate." The new version appears in the version bar, with a note on what changed from the previous version. If you go back to an old version and keep editing, a new branch is split off automatically. Other branches show a row of small thumbnails at the fork point, which you can click to expand in place. Hover over a thumbnail to see the large image, or hover elsewhere to see a full comparison with the previous version. You can keep queuing while generating. The random pool draws a different artist combination or action for each image, so generating 20 images gives 20 combinations.

When there are many branches, open the **Branch Overview**. It lays out all of the work's branches on one canvas, one row per branch, with lines connecting each branch to the version it split from. Like viewing a large image, you can zoom with the scroll wheel and drag to move. Zoom out to see the structure, or zoom in to see every image and change for each version. You can find versions by tag, collapse branches, navigate with the minimap, and hold Ctrl and click two versions to compare them directly. Even with hundreds of versions, it stays orderly.

## Edit images without leaving the software

A row of actions appears below each image: upscale, enhance, inpainting, outpainting, plus director tools such as background removal, colorization, and expression change. Each one shows its size and price before you run it, and the result is a new version that you can compare side by side with the original or overlay on it.

LarryE135/dsh-flash-presets.description: Reducing Token consumption of Deepseek v4.1flash / Raising Token efficiency without lossing performance (Works for v4.1flash)
LarryE135/dsh-flash-presets.body:
# dsh-flash-presets

Agent presets for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), tuned for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

It does something simple: it compresses context earlier, keeps only the head and tail of overly long tool outputs, leaves unused tools out of the system prompt, and merges scattered tool calls into a single `run_code` where possible. The model does not become smarter as a result. What changes is how much a session reads, how many detours it takes, and when it wraps up.

The whole package ships as a DSH bundle (`dsh.bundle`): it inserts preset lines into the profile without changing host code or touching the shared tool registry.

> Current version: v0.2.6 (2026-11-06) · Presets v3 lite / v3 balance · Plan mode plan-mode v1 (1.0.0) · Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc; tested with 0.2.1-rc.5 and 0.2.2-rc.1
>
> The latest version on npm is still 0.2.5, which cannot create new sessions on DSH 0.2.2-rc.1. Until 0.2.6 is published to npm, install from GitHub or the Release attachments (see [Installation](#安装)).

## Who it's for and who it isn't

**Good fit**

- Tasks with clear goals and acceptance criteria: changing code, running scripts, organizing data, producing deliverables in a specified format.
- Long sessions. The default compression threshold is 80% of context, which most sessions never reach. This preset lowers it to 25%, so long-session context stays within a manageable range.
- People who care about their token bill and don't want to repeat instructions to the model in every message.

**Not a good fit**

- Problems clearly beyond the model's ability, such as competition-level problems where the goal is partial credit. For these tasks, standard mode is more stable; see [Unfavorable results](#不利的结果).
- Workflows that depend on the current date, plugin installation within a conversation, or scheduled tasks. These capabilities are removed in this preset (see [Differences from the official PTC preset](#与官方-ptc-预设的差异)).
- Models other than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. The rules may still be useful, but they have not been validated.
- DSH 0.2.0 and earlier. Use the corresponding older version instead (see [Version and compatibility](https://github.com/LarryE135/dsh-flash-presets/blob/HEAD/docs/版本与兼容性.md)). Directory-style presets from before DSH 0.1.7 are no longer provided in 0.2.6.

## What it does

Four mechanisms act on four different moments in a session and do not overlap:

| Mechanism | Moment it acts | Settings | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn compression | When the context stock is too large | `thresholdRatio: 0.25`, `retainTokens: 20000` (official default 0.8) | History is replaced with a summary; triggers only in long sessions |
| Tool output trimming | …

# ModAVD (modified AVD)

An Android emulator based on AOSP Android Emulator 37.2.10, with a set of patches applied and then compiled by us. It currently supports Windows, and more platforms are planned (see [#27](https://github.com/ModAVD/ModAVD/issues/27)).

The package includes the manager `ModAVD.exe` and the command-line tool `tools\\modavd.exe`, for creating instances and starting and stopping them. It can also be connected to automation tools such as [AUTO-MAS](https://github.com/AUTO-MAS-Project/AUTO-MAS), which handle instance orchestration and task workflows.

**Documentation site: <https://modavd.github.io/>** (installation, upgrades, feedback, privacy, and notes on each component and on contributing are all there)

> **Version note (current Release vs `main`)**: This document is written for the latest published full package, `v0.38.1`. `main` may contain changes that have not yet shipped in a Release. When using a downloaded package, follow the notes for the corresponding Release and the version inside the package.

- [What is this](#这是什么)
- [Supported environments](#适用环境)
- [Installation](#安装)
- [Upgrade](#升级)
- [License and source code](#许可证与源码)
- [Feedback](#反馈)
- [Privacy](#隐私)
- [Disclaimer](#免责声明)
- [Icons and artwork](#图标与美术)

## What is this

- An Android emulator that currently runs on Windows and uses the Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) for hardware acceleration. More platforms are planned.
- It can open a window and be used like a regular emulator, or run without a window (headless), launched by the manager, the command line, or scripts, and shut down when finished.
- The emulator itself comes from Google's open-source [Android Emulator](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/qemu/). We modified its QEMU, gfxstream (graphics forwarding), and Crashpad (crash handling) components. The changes are published as patches (`patches/`).
- adb and the Android system images belong to Google and are subject to the Android Software Development Kit License Agreement, so we cannot redistribute them and they are not included in the Release. Instead, the manager's "Complete components" feature (or the command `tools\\modavd.exe components fetch`) downloads them to your computer from official sources.

Compared with the official emulator, the published 0.38.1 build no longer uploads usage statistics and crash reports to Google, and does not send to Google…

SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now.description: Let AI see your screen in real time: frames are filtered by how much they change and several frames are tiled into one image; a static screen costs almost no tokens
SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now.body:
# See Now · Let AI See Your Screen in Real Time

> **AI no longer "listens to you describe the screen". It looks for itself, and only sends the frames where the picture has changed.**

A real-time vision plugin for [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) that turns your screen (or camera / video file) into a stream of frames filtered by how much they change, packs several of those frames into one image, and hands it to the model.

A static screen costs almost nothing. A one-take video gets frames based on how much motion there is. A hard-cut slideshow keeps one frame per cut.

---

## License

**Apache License 2.0**: use it freely. Personal use, internal company use, closed-source products, SaaS, and redistribution are all allowed. **You don't need to ask me for permission, and it's free.** You only need to keep the [LICENSE](https://github.com/SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now/blob/HEAD/LICENSE) and [NOTICE](https://github.com/SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now/blob/HEAD/NOTICE) files.

If you feel it saved you time, you're welcome to scan the QR code to tip. It's purely voluntary and **doesn't change anything above**:

Before submitting a PR, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md). **No CLA signature is required now**. Just follow the Apache-2.0 rules.

---

## What it looks like

Debug window (for development only, not in the release package): the left side shows **every captured frame**. Kept frames show a thumbnail and a grid number; dropped frames leave only a score bar. The right side shows **the image being assembled**, placed at its real pixel positions. A new frame flashes when it lands in a cell, and cells slide when the layout is rearranged.

Per-scene mode (`scene:true`): each scene change produces its own full-frame image. The "Generated" panel in the bottom right marks every entry with `1 frame 100%`.

Floating window: what the AI says appears here and is read aloud (`say` is the only channel).

You can change the appearance under **Settings › Watch what you watch › Floating window style**: `Live glass` (follows the desktop blur, uses CPU), `Static frosted` (doesn't capture the screen, CPU near 0; pick this if things feel laggy), `Solid color`, and `Auto`. Changes take effect immediately, with no need to restart DSH. It shares the same `~/.dsh/watch-window.json` with the watch-along feature.

---

## What problem it solves

The most obvious way to have AI watch your screen with you is to "take a full screenshot on a timer and feed it in". That runs into two dead ends:

| Approach | Problem |
|---|---|
| Full screenshot every 2 seconds | 30 images per minute, nearly all duplicates. Tokens burn through fast |
| Full screenshot every 30 seconds | Everything that happened in between is lost, and the AI can only say "looks like you're using a computer" |

See Now…

Selection and deployment assets for **connecting DeepSeek Harness (DSH) to QQ**: which path to take, how to accept it, and which pitfalls others have already hit.

**The sole standard: it should feel like a real person in QQ.** Not "the feature is connected," but "send a message, get a response within seconds, you can interrupt it, the group isn't flooded, and errors are explained in plain language." Metrics are in the [UX spec](https://github.com/ahandsomeboy6666/dsh-qq-cookbook/blob/HEAD/docs/07-ux-spec.md).

> No code relationship with [qq-bridge](https://github.com/Derpyu520/qq-bridge); it is referenced only as a source of verified conclusions, serving as a factual baseline.
>

### 🔍 1. Detection System (Detection Core)
* **scan `/proc/self/maps`** — checks the process's memory mapping list (`sub_4DA108` decodes the strings `"/proc/self/maps"` and `"rb"`)

* **hook check (PLT / inline)** — checks for modifications to the GOT/PLT tables or ARM64 instruction patches in the middle of a function
* **GG / Frida / ptrace check** — detects memory scanners, hooking frameworks, and debugger attachment (`sub_259670`)
* **abnormal syscall check** — checks for abnormal System Call invocations via the Dynamic Syscall Dispatcher (`sub_4A9A00`)

# travel-planner —— Travel Assistant Skill (Itinerary Planning + Public Transit + Weather)

This packages "travel" as an AI skill. Once loaded, the model knows which command to run, how to pass its parameters, which fields in the output are directly usable, and which pitfalls to avoid.

> Skill name `travel-planner`; repository name `travel-planner`.
> **Zero third-party dependencies, zero API keys**: just install python3 and it runs.

## Core Idea

A trip is not four unrelated features. It is **a journey made up of several legs**:

```
Origin ──[train/high-speed rail]──→ Arrival station ──[metro/bus]──→ Destination ──[walk]──→ Attraction
                            ↑                    ↑
                    first/last train bottlenecks        weather, alerts, fares
```

So the main entry point is **`transit.py journey`**. It links 12306 train tickets, metro transfers in 55 cities, real-time bus data in 579 cities, and China Weather Network weather alerts into **a single timeline with times**, and performs cross-mode checks (transfer buffers, last-train bottlenecks, weather alerts).

## Features

- 🧭 **End-to-end trip orchestration**: train + metro + bus + weather combined into one timeline; supports `--arrive-by` for working backward from an arrival time
- 🚄 **Train tickets**: 12306 seat availability, timetables, and seat classes (standard library implementation)

- 🚌 **Real-time bus**: live vehicle positions on a line, **arrival predictions (stops and minutes remaining)**, routes serving a stop, direct routes, citywide scan
- 🌤️ **Weather**: current conditions + AQI + **life indices (clothing / travel / exercise / UV…)** + weather alerts + 7-day forecast + hourly forecast (China Weather Network)
- 🗺️ **Attraction planning**: built-in attraction library (ratings / tickets / tags / visit duration), with automatic daily itinerary generation
- 🍽️ **Food recommendations**: built-in food price guide for five cities
- 📊 **Multiple budget levels**: budget / comfortable / premium
- 📱 **Xiaohongshu guides**: 88 built-in popular recommendation posts for five cities, including pitfalls to avoid

# XStats

**Mac system monitoring and common tools, with both a main window and a menu bar experience.**

CPU, memory, network, and temperature at a glance; expand to view trends and per-app usage. AI, calendar, fan control, and other tools can be enabled as needed.

[Download latest version](https://github.com/ysicing/xstats/releases) · [Features](#功能) · [Installation](#安装) · [Data & Privacy](#数据与隐私) · [Changelog](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)

[Simplified Chinese](#) · [English](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) · [Japanese](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/README.ja.md) · [Korean](https://github.com/ysicing/XStats/blob/HEAD/README.ko.md)

## Features

XStats is built natively with Swift, AppKit, and SwiftUI. It is free and open source, and requires no account registration.

### Menu bar layout

Metrics can be **displayed independently**, shown in **aggregated mode**, or combined into a single **three-in-one icon** with freely arranged content. In icon-only mode, the Dock icon also shows the same live status. Displayed items, order, and style (text, icons, rings, progress bars, history charts) are all customizable.

Aggregated mode lets you choose items separately for the menu bar and the status overview. In the overview, you can view metrics together and open details.

The menu bar layout and status overview use demo data, so different layouts and information combinations can be showcased.

### On-demand features and menu bar display

Under "Settings → Features", basic monitoring and optional features are managed separately.

- **Basic monitoring**: CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, energy, and fans can each be turned off. When turned off, real-time collection, related alerts, and new history records stop. Basic information, page entry points, and existing history are retained. System widgets still refresh independently.
- **Menu bar display**: Except for the battery info entry, when "Show in menu bar" is checked for basic monitoring, AI, or audio, the corresponding feature is also enabled. Unchecking it only removes the entry and does not disable the feature. AI and audio also have separate display options.
- **Display parameter control**: Only controls reading and writing of brightness, contrast, and volume. When turned off, you can still view display information and separately choose whether to show it in the menu bar.

### System monitoring

| Module | Content |
|---|---|
| **CPU** | User / system / idle usage, per-core and core-group load, load average, frequency and temperature, thermal pressure alerts |
| **GPU** | Graphics load, core count, temperature and power draw |
| **Memory** | Memory pressure, app / compressed / cached composition, swap space and swap-in/swap-out rates |
| **Disk** | Capacity, read/write rates, per-app read/write ranking, SMART health information |
|…
